life_summary: Robert Dean Hales was born August 24, 1932, in New York City to a family with business and civic connections. He earned his bachelor's degree in business administration and developed a successful career in accounting and business administration. Hales served in the United States Air Force, where he gained additional leadership experience and discipline that shaped his approach to church service. He married Mary Crandall on June 10, 1953, in the Salt Lake Temple, and together they raised two sons. The Hales family maintained strong community ties throughout their lives, and Robert became known for his emphasis on the practical application of church welfare principles and his integrity in financial stewardship.
church_summary: Hales was called as a general authority in 1975 as an Assistant to the Quorum of the Twelve, serving in the First Quorum of the Seventy from 1976 to 1985. He was then appointed Presiding Bishop of the Church from 1985 to 1994, overseeing the church's extensive welfare program and administrative operations. He was ordained as an apostle on April 7, 1994, and served in the Quorum of the Twelve until his death in 2017. Hales was heavily involved in church expansion in Europe, including work on the development of the East Germany Temple and the Manhattan New York Temple. His ministry consistently emphasized the importance of the church's welfare program and helping members achieve self-reliance.
